title: Writing a post in the admin panel, as a full page
question: New post (and opening any post on the Church news desk or a ministry's News) becomes its own page: the post's blocks at a reading width, Write and Preview on a phone as tabs (your answer), Cancel bottom left and Post bottom right. Where should who it's for, the notification, when and the link go? A second question, how text editing itself should work, follows on this page after you pick.

options.label: Who, when and telling along the top
options.thesis: Four summary tiles across the top (Who it's for, Notification, When, Link at the end), each opening its settings in place; the post below at a 760px reading width with Write and Preview tabs; the save bar across the foot.
options.viewport: New post: the four tiles, then Write chosen, the title, a text block formatted in place, a gallery, the Add row; Cancel and Post for everyone at the foot.
options.risk: Settings are summaries you open one by one, so checking them all is four clicks.

options.label: The post as a page, its settings beside it
options.thesis: The post sits as a white page on sand at a 760px reading width with Write and Preview tabs; every setting is open in a column on the right (Who it's for, Send a notification, When, A link at the end), with Cancel and Post at that column's foot.
options.viewport: The page with Write chosen, title, text block, gallery, heading and Add row; on the right the four settings groups and Cancel / Post for everyone.
options.risk: The busiest of the three, and on a laptop the page narrows to make room for the column.

options.label: A tab for each part
options.thesis: Three tabs across the top: Write, Preview on a phone, and Who, when and telling (its tab summing them up); the post alone at a 720px width while writing, and the save bar at the foot repeating the summary beside Post.
options.viewport: Write chosen, the post centred: title, text block, gallery, heading, Add row; Everyone · Notification on · Now beside Post for everyone.
options.risk: The settings are out of sight while writing, so a wrong audience is easier to miss.
